subject: Regional peering outage — automated traffic shift and customer runbook
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Ramirez <sophie.ramirez@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-09-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Incident: Peering exchange disruption affecting us-east and eu-west — automated shift initiated

Hi Sophie,

Quick summary: at 08:05 PDT we observed a partial peering outage affecting the primary exchange for us-east and eu-west regions. Our serving runtime detected elevated packet loss on the exchange and automatically activated the regional traffic-shift policy for affected tenants. For Acme Retail we initiated a non-invasive reroute to our alternate regional gateways (edge-gw-2/us-east and edge-gw-3/eu-west) to preserve requests behind the same logical endpoint.

What you may have seen: brief 5–20s spikes of 502s for long-lived streaming connections and higher tail latency for short text generation requests. The automated shift completed for most traffic within ~30s.

Actions we've taken (already done):
- Switched tenants to alternate peering paths via automatic routing policy.
- Increased KV-prefetch timeout for ongoing requests to prevent early failures.
- Kept cache priming on fallback gateways to reduce cold-token latency.

Recommended immediate customer actions:
- If you have pinned DNS TTLs in front of Redwood, please avoid lowering TTL further until we confirm full restoration — doing so may cause unnecessary flapping.
- For clients relying on web sockets, re-establish logic to tolerate a single short disconnect; we will not force session termination.
- Optional: enable our sidecar fallback (instructions attached) if you want traffic split to a secondary region for the next 24–48 hours.

Attachments: acme_action_checklist.pdf (short checklist), regional-traffic-shift-playbook.csv (automated rules we applied).

We are actively investigating root cause with the exchange operator and our network partners. I will keep you updated via this thread and the incident page: https://status.redwood.in/company/incident/2029-09-01

Ben
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sophie Ramirez <sophie.ramirez@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2029-09-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident: Peering exchange disruption affecting us-east and eu-west — automated shift initiated

Internal note for SRE/action owners — copying Sophie for transparency.

Short answers for Sophie (paste-friendly):
- Streaming sessions: most sessions will reconnect automatically; for the small subset that timed out during the 5–20s window, clients should replay the last in-flight event. We did not intentionally drop sessions but TCP resets at the exchange may have terminated a minority of connections.
- SLA credits: we will follow our standard SLA review process. Please open a ticket with billing@redwood.ai referencing Acme Retail and link to hubspot:deal_67219. We will queue a post-incident SLA evaluation after root cause.

Action items (internal):
1) Karthik — confirm if persistent connections were held for Acme tenant ids (10021, 10022) on fallback GW and provide percentage of reconnects.
2) Marissa — prepare a 1-page customer summary and credit process note for Sophie.
3) SRE (cc: soojin_lee) — collect tcpdump + exchange logs for 08:00–08:10 window, mark time slices, and upload to shared drive.

I will send a concise runbook and checklist once we have SRE artifacts.

Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2029-09-01T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident: Peering exchange disruption affecting us-east and eu-west — automated shift initiated

Quick update:
- For tenant 10021 and 10022 (Acme): ~96% of TCP sessions reconnected within 12s on the fallback GW. ~4% required client-initiated reconnects (replay recommended).
- We collected pcaps and exchange-side logs and pushed artifacts to the drive (link below).
- Root cause: preliminary is a BGP flap at the exchange due to a misconfigured route reflector; network partner is rolling a configuration change.
- No action required from Acme to recover traffic; we recommend enabling the sidecar fallback if you want split traffic for resilience while the exchange config is being corrected.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyExampleSharedDrive

Karthik
Sr. Network Reliability Engineer

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Ramirez <sophie.ramirez@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-09-03T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident: regional peering exchange — customer summary and next steps

Hi Sophie — follow-up and short post-incident summary. Apologies again for the disruption. We completed our internal triage and wanted to share the timeline and next steps you can expect from us.

What happened (brief):
- 08:00–08:08 PDT 2029-09-01: BGP route reflector misconfiguration at the exchange caused transient packet loss and TCP resets into our primary peering fabric for us-east and eu-west.
- 08:05: automated traffic-shift policy triggered for affected tenants, completing within ~30s.
- 08:10–09:00: gradual stabilization while partner rolled config correction.

Impact to Acme:
- Brief 502s and increased tail latency for <1% of requests; ~4% of streaming sessions required client reconnects and replay.
- No customer data exposure.

What we did for you:
- Executed automated reroute and KV-cache priming to limit cold starts.
- Collected pcaps and exchange logs; artifacts are in the shared drive.
- Created and attached a one-page customer checklist (acme_action_checklist.pdf) and the exact automated rules applied (regional-traffic-shift-playbook.csv).

Next steps and timeline:
- Today: we will run a teardown test with the exchange operator to validate the config change.
- Within 72 hours: final postmortem doc and proposed SLA credit (if eligible) will be shared.
- Optional: If you want, we can enable persistent sidecar fallback for 48 hours to keep a subset of traffic on secondary peering; this is non-disruptive and reversible.

If you want us to proceed with sidecar fallback for Acme, reply with "OPT-IN SIDE CAR" and we will kick it off immediately.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll follow up with the formal postmortem and credit process.

Ben
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
